UNIT I 
 
Introduction to H uman resource Management 
(HRM)  
Human Resource Management is the process of managing people in an 
organization so that their abilities, knowledge, and efforts contribute 
effectively to organizational goals. Modern organizations increasingly 
recognize that machines, technology, and capita l alone cannot ensure 
success; it is people who create innovation, productivity, and competitive 
advantage.  
In earlier times, employees were often viewed merely as a workforce 
used to perform tasks. Over time, organizations realized that employees 
are valuable assets whose skills, creativity, commitment, and motivation 
determine the long -term growth of the organ ization. As a result, 
personnel administration gradually evolved into the broader and more 
strategic concept of Human Resource Management.  
HRM is concerned not only with hiring employees but also with 
developing their potential, maintaining good relations, ensuring fair 
compensation, improving performance, and creating a positive work 
environment. It seeks to balance organizational objectives  with 
employee needs and aspirations.  
In today’s global and technology -driven economy, HRM has become a 
strategic function. Organizations such as Google and Tata Consultancy 
Services invest heavily in employee development, leadership, 
engagement, and workplace culture because talented and moti vated 
employees are considered the most important source of sustainable 
success.  
Thus, HRM plays a vital role in acquiring the right people, developing 
their capabilities, motivating them to perform, and retaining them for the 
long-term success of the organization.  
 
 
 
Definitions of HRM  
According to Edwin.  B. Flippo  
Human resource management is the Planning,  Organizing,  
Directing and controlling of the Procurement,  development, 
compensation,  integration,  maintenance and separation of human 
resources to the end that individual,  organizational and societal 
objectives are accom plished . 
 
• Objectives of HRM  
 
1) Achieve organizational goals  
It is one the fundamental objective of HRM.  The organization has to 
ensure that right people with right skills are available in the right jobs at 
the right time . It aims to align the individual employee goals with the 
larger organisational objectives . 
2) Optimum Utilization of HR  
The skills,  knowledge and capabilities of the human resources 
need to tapped and utilised to the maximum potential properly so 
that they can effectively contribute to  the organization.  
3) Employee satisfaction and Development  
One of the prima ry aims  of the HRM is to make sure that their 
employees are satisfied and motivated. By  providing better 
wages, Salary  and benefits , the workforce would feel contented 
and this leads to job satisfaction and boosts their morale to 
become more productive day

Document: HRPM UNIT II MATERIAL_.pdf
UNIT II  
 
Human Resource Development (HRD)  
Introduction  
Human Resource Development (HRD)  is a continuous process of improving the 
knowledge, skills, abilities, attitudes, and competencies of employees to enhance 
their performance and prepare them for future responsibilities. HRD focuses on 
employee growth, career development, and organization al effectiveness by creating 
a learning -oriented work environment.  
Definition (Leonard Nadler):  
"Human Resource Development is a series of organized activities conducted 
within a specified time to produce behavioural change and improve employee 
performance."  
 
Objectives of HRD  
1. Improve Employee Knowledge and Skills  
To enhance employees' competencies through continuous learning and 
development.  
2. Increase Employee Performance  
To improve individual and organizational productivity.  
3. Prepare Future Leaders  
To develop employees for higher positions and future responsibilities.  
4. Enhance Job Satisfaction  
To improve employee motivation, morale, and commitment.  
5. Support Organizational Growth  
To align employee development with organizational goals and future needs.  
6. Promote Continuous Learning  
To encourage employees to continuously upgrade their knowledge and skills.  
 
 
Importance of HRD  
• Improves employee productivity.  
• Develops future leaders.  
• Increases employee motivation and morale.  
• Reduces employee turnover.  
• Encourages innovation and creativity.  
• Improves organizational competitiveness.  
• Supports career growth and succession planning.  
 
Elements of HRD  
1. Training and Development  
Training improves employees' current job skills, while development prepares them 
for future responsibilities. HRD organizes training programmes, workshops, 
seminars, and skill  development activities to enhance employee competence.  
 
2. Performance Appraisal  
Performance appraisal is the systematic evaluation of employee performance. It 
helps identify strengths, weaknesses, training needs, promotions, rewards, and 
areas for improvement.  
 
3. Career Planning  
Career planning helps employees identify career goals and provides opportunities for 
career growth through promotions, transfers, mentoring, and development 
programmes.  
 
4. Leadership Development  
Leadership development focuses on preparing employees for managerial and 
leadership roles. HRD develops decision -making, communication, problem -solving, 
and leadership skills through coaching and mentoring.  
 
5. Talent Management  
Talent management involves attracting, developing, retaining, and utilizing talented 
employees. It ensures that high -performing employees are identified and prepared 
for key positions within the organization.  
 
6. Knowledge Management  
Knowledge management is the process of creating, sharing, storing, and utilizing  
organizational knowledge. HRD encourages employees to exchange ideas, best  
practices, and experiences to improve innovation and or
